title: Merit-order curves of available aFRR/mFRR energy bids per quarter-hour on a fixed MW grid.
transformation_notes: Built from ODS156 (incremental = direction up) and ODS157 (decremental = direction down) individual energy bids; only bids with availability == 'Available' are used. Raw bid rows are not redistributed.
Bid volumes are the increments of Elia's published cumulativevolume in its merit-order rank, so bids that add no volume (mutually exclusive alternatives, unavailable bids) are excluded.

Per quarter-hour and direction the available aFRR + mFRR (+ reserve-sharing) bids are sorted by price into an economic merit order: cheapest first for up (incremental), highest price first for down (decremental). price_eur_mwh at cum_mw = V is the price of the bid that covers the V-th MW, i.e. the marginal price needed to activate V MW. Null where the available volume is below V. Grid: 0..2000 MW in 25 MW steps.
Elia's own rank (aFRR first, then mFRR) was tested as an alternative ordering and tracks the published MIP/MDP much worse (see validation.curve_vs_published_prices for the price-sorted curve).

Approximation: real aFRR activations are continuous and priced via PICASSO cross-border marginal prices, mFRR via MARI, and Elia may skip bids (e.g. for congestion); treat the curve as a stylised local merit order for price-impact studies, not as the settlement price.
